category: udp port forward (self-hostable server, managed cloud)

free_tier.stated: Create a free account and generate an auth token; self-hosting is free under AGPL. The managed cloud is pay-as-you-go from USD 3/month.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel or an address, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Managed service offers pay-as-you-go from $3/mo with idle time free. Self-hosting has no quota on self-hosted infrastructure.; ingress: udp

interface_detail: mytunnel client, a live dashboard, Prometheus metrics and an audit log
tooling: mytunnel client from brew or a binary, self-hostable server in Rust
chaining: self-hosting on a free VM turns this into a free UDP relay; the managed cloud does not

limits.value: no free byte allowance published; the managed cloud is metered and billed from USD 3/month

binding_note: A metered service with no published free allowance binds on bytes by construction: at one TiB a month the account is a paying customer. Self-hosting moves the cost to a VM, which is a compute-lane answer rather than an egress answer.

identity_cost.detail: a free account and a generated auth token: 'Access to the hosted service requires an auth token. Create a free account and generate one yourself.' https://www.rustunnel.com/docs/quickstart.md

reliability_note: sessions are reaped after 60 seconds of inactivity, which suits WireGuard keepalive but means an idle peer is torn down
confidence_note: The UDP mechanics and the pay-as-you-go price are read from the vendor's own pages. The openness is the free-account sentence with no allowance behind it. Raise by signing up free, running mytunnel udp against a listener, and reading whether a port is allocated and whether it survives a restart.

evidence.proved: UDP tunnels exist, the public port comes from a dedicated UDP range, sessions are reaped after 60 seconds of inactivity
'Pay-as-you-go from $3/mo - idle time always free. Or self-host free under AGPL', plus 'Start free' and 'free self-hosting under AGPL'
'Create a free account' and 'Access to the hosted service requires an auth token'; no allowance stated

notes: Fast reverse tunnel in Rust supporting TCP and UDP forwarding. Hosted service is priced on usage; software is open source and self-hostable.

extras.wg_detail: UDP tunnels are real and documented: 'rustunnel UDP tunnels forward datagrams from a public port on the tunnel server to a local UDP service', with 'Public port - allocated from a dedicated UDP port range on the server' and a 60-second session idle timeout. Whether a free hosted account gets a port, and whether the port is fixed, is not stated. https://www.rustunnel.com/docs/reference/udp-tunnels.md
extras.volume_stated: No free byte allowance is published anywhere read today. The managed service is 'Pay-as-you-go from $3/mo - idle time always free'; self-hosting has no quota because it is the operator's own server.
extras.transit_note: the managed relay carries the datagrams, or the self-hosted server does
